subject: Data Engineering
title: The Big Three: AWS, GCP, Azure
description: A micro-lesson that makes The Big Three: AWS, GCP, Azure usable.

hook.text: Three companies control most of the world's cloud infrastructure. Their data ecosystems define the market.

buildup.text: AWS launched first with S3 and Redshift. Azure followed with enterprise integrations. GCP brought BigQuery.

discovery.text: Each cloud offers equivalent services: object storage, warehouses, streaming, and orchestration tools.

twist.text: Vendor lock-in is the hidden cost. Migrating a petabyte data pipeline between clouds is a multi-year project.

climax.text: Choosing a cloud provider is less about technology and more about existing contracts and team expertise.

punchline.text: Pick a cloud. But know the exit costs.

quiz.question: What is the hidden cost of choosing a single cloud provider?
options: Vendor lock-in makes migration extremely expensive
All three clouds have identical pricing
